title: Compare padding controls with matched smoothing and unseen works
statement: On the three cleaned independent work pairs from P-J-011, choose source order 0–8 on the first 48 training-work blocks against the next 16, then refit on the 64 and evaluate once on the first 64 blocks of the other work. Order 3 is selected in all three. Constant letter-padding forward per-source bits are 3.355, 3.150, 3.249 (Latin, Italian, German); an alignment-aware model using the last three source symbols and their emitted markers yields 3.065, 2.985, 2.962. The source inverse benchmark is 3.224, 3.034, 3.184. The aligned and forward models have different smoothing and state, so these differences are not a controlled causal estimate of context length alone. For a matched random permutation of B/D markers the inverse benchmark bills per-block log2 binomial choices, yielding 3.997, 3.819, 3.965 bits per original symbol. All transformed blocks invert exactly. For constant suffix, a known-rule decoder tracks whether the preceding source symbol is a letter: it maps a source-space prediction to B followed by a forced space and emits the final B at the known block boundary. It uses exactly the original source model bits; conventional forward suffix results are included.
check: Repeat on independently selected works and genres and compare models with identical state-specific interpolation and priors, varying only whether the context reaches the same number of source symbols. Test multiple marker randomizations and order-selection folds. Bill the model, transform and boundary metadata if they are not shared; use distinct markers or explicitly code alignment when they collide with source symbols. Do not interpret a smaller finite-model rate as a reduction in joint information.

methods.selection: 48 consecutive training-work blocks fit, next 16 validate source Markov order, refit 64; first 64 blocks of separate evaluation work. The validation split was fixed before these results; same works as P-J-011, so these are not new work-pair replications.
methods.source: P-J-011 cleaned extraction scripts and source metadata; symbols a-z plus space; block ends and rules known to encoder and decoder.
methods.aligned: For source and marker events separately, condition on the last n source symbols and their markers, and for a marker include its just-emitted source character. Add-0.5 unigram and context interpolation prior mass 2. Marker location follows from the prior decoded source character; distinct B/D alphabet and known transform make alignment free under these assumptions.
methods.forward: P-J-011 interpolated Markov character model at n output symbols, not n source symbols; additive unigram .5 and interpolated shorter contexts with prior mass 2.
methods.random: Per-block shuffled exact deterministic-marker histogram, seeded independently by block and split. The inverse benchmark bills log2 binomial(n,k) per block, conditioned on recovered source and known rule. Marker sequence is not given to decoder.
methods.limitations: The source and aligned estimators differ in smoothing, fitted parameterization and event-state conditioning; direct rate differences combine those effects. Counts are predictive code lengths, not measured compression files; model descriptions, transform rules, block boundaries and source alphabet are treated as shared. Single validation partition, one random draw per block; not manuscript evidence.

suffix_boundary_state.description: At a source prediction after a letter, relabel probability of space as B then force space. At end of block emit B free. Else emit the source symbol. The decoder tracks whether previous source symbol was a letter; rule and block ends are shared.

reproduction.instruction: Extract the three script strings from experiments/P-J-011/mubadala777/step.json reproduction.scripts to a temporary directory; run extract_works.py with PYTHONPATH pointing at repository root. Put this script beside them as matched.py; adapt its absolute /tmp/voy-entropy paths to that directory, and run with both directories on PYTHONPATH. Input pins are SHA-verified by the extractor.
